propositions: JiraConfig accepts non-https (http://) URLs without validation, risking API token/basic-auth credential exposure in transit over cleartext.
Three config consumers (resolve_jira_settings, _jira_onboard._detect, write_jira_config) silently swallow ConfigError, bypassing scheme validation and allowing unsafe URLs to persist.
DC's ReconcilerConfig rejects non-https base_url via __post_init__ and _validate_reconciler_tls; Cloud's JiraConfig lacks equivalent validation, inconsistent with fail-loud design.
write_jira_config persists jira.url without scheme validation, enabling onboarding to silently write a cleartext URL to the config file.

Resolution requires: (1) extracting shared _validate_https_url validator; (2) adding allow_insecure bool to JiraConfig with __post_init__ enforcement; (3) re-raising InsecureUrlError in resolve_jira_settings before catching ConfigError; (4) validating scheme in write_jira_config before persist.
